about.text:
Renade stood for solidarity, justice, and warmth.

On 28.08.2025 at around 2:16 a.m., she passed away peacefully — surrounded by dear people.

This page gathers memories and shares ways of remembering her.

The fundraising phase has now ended. Thanks to great solidarity, a dignified burial in the forest cemetery (Friedwald) at Burg Plesse — at Renade’s chosen resting place next to her friend Lena — was made possible.

quotes.text:
Göttingen,
Um 2:16 Uhr ist dein Herz stehen geblieben.
Die Stimme deiner Straße ist stumm.
Deine Seele ist frei.
Die Liebe die du dieser Welt gestiftet hast bleibt
Und wir machen weiter für dich.
In Liebe zu dir
#renade

Renade

Nen Mensch wie dich den trifft man leider
Nicht so oft im Leben
Wo Alte-Weiße-Männer-Neide
Gern den Ton vorgeben
Denn denen passt ein Mensch wie du
Oft nicht in ihre Suppe
Denn wer dich kennt dem sind im Nu
Die Obermacker Schnuppe
Bei jeder Demo Stets dabei
Bei jeder Soliküche
Bringt Chunks und Stampf und Reis und Brei
Auf vollgeklebte Tische
Und wär auf dieser weiten Welt
Nur ein Prozent dir ähnlich
Bräuchts weder Politik noch Geld
Das Paradies wärs nämlich

quotes.author: ThOP Ensemble
quotes.text:
Dear current and former ThOP people, dear friends of Renate,

Quiet — she certainly wasn’t, our Renate! You could hear her coming from afar, her voice always resonated throughout the ThOP. Now it has fallen silent, but its echo will accompany us for a long time.

On the night of 28.08.2025, our long-time collaborator Renate Hillebrandt (Renade) passed away after a short and serious illness.

Her absence tears a hole in our midst. We are incredibly sad.

quotes.author: Internationales Mittwochskoch
quotes.text:
Renade — cook and reliable jack-of-all-trades

We wanted to cook — for 20, 50, 80, or 150 people. The first hand to shoot up was Renade’s — "I’m in, when should I be there...?" She always already had a suggestion for what would be good to cook for the occasion. At the Wednesday kitchen, she was firmly part of the kitchen crew and had a large share in the steady success of those sociable evenings.

Anyone who knew Renade also knows that she was a critical voice on gender justice and other injustices, and that she rightly paid attention and spoke up when things were going wrong. Renade was part of the neighborhood activists’ assembly and, for example, organized our information booth against domestic violence.

Distributing the Masch Courier, baking cakes for the Mit-Ma(s)ch Café or the flea market, helping at the OM10 construction site, resisting the patriarchy: you could count on Renade — always — sadly no longer a given today.

Now she is no longer here... Renade has gone — for good. She passed away quietly and peacefully in the circle of many friends.

Renade remains an inspiration to us all; she lives on in us, in our actions and ideas. That makes us glad.

It may be a comforting thought that Renade is sitting with a smile in a celestial kitchen, cooking a tasty little soup for Curt Cobain, Janis Joplin, and Rio Reiser.

Take care, dear human...
